buildNote: Phase 7 (Entry Points) complete. Created fruster-user-service.ts (verbatim port of fruster-user-service.js: ~30 bus.subscribe() calls registering all handlers, conditional registration for useDbRolesAndScopes / profile-splitting / useMeEndpoint / non-mock expressApp.start, createIndexes() function). Created app.ts (verbatim port of app.js with the one intentional API change: `require('fruster-health').start()` -> `startHealth(bus)` per @fruster/health's new signature requiring the bus instance, confirmed against node_modules/@fruster/health/dist/index.d.ts: `start: (bus?: typeof frusterBus) => Promise<void>`). Confirmed via node_modules/@fruster/bus/dist/lib/FrusterBus.d.ts that `bus.subscribe(options)` takes the same SubscribeOptions shape as the legacy fruster-bus (subject/permissions/requestSchema/responseSchema/docs/handle/mustBeLoggedIn/deprecated) -- no API change needed for subscribe wiring itself, only the previously-found bus.publish() options-object change (which doesn't appear in this file; this file only subscribes). expressApp kept as `require('./web/express-app')` with `// @ts-ignore` since web/ is excluded from tsconfig and stays CommonJS. MongoClient connect call dropped the `{ useNewUrlParser, useUnifiedTopology }` options object (no-op/default in mongodb@4.17.2, confirmed in package.json) -- behavior-identical, sanctioned by the plan's own note for this task. FULL GRAPH TYPE-CHECK CHECKPOINT: `npx tsc --noEmit` initially surfaced 2 real type errors that only appear once the full app->service->handlers->managers->repos import graph compiles together (these were invisible during Phase 1-6 per-file glob compilation): (1) line ~157 `constants.schemas.request.REMOVE_SYSTEM_ROLE_SCOPES` does not exist (real key is `REMOVE_SYSTEM_ROLE_SCOPES_REQUEST`), (2) line ~309 `constants.schemas.request.USER_RESPONSE` does not exist (USER_RESPONSE only exists under `schemas.response`, not `schemas.request`). Verified via grep against the original fruster-user-service.js that these are PRE-EXISTING TYPOS in the original untyped JS (lines 157 and 309 in the .js use the exact same wrong property paths), meaning requestSchema/responseSchema silently resolved to `undefined` at runtime for the REMOVE_SYSTEM_ROLE_SCOPES (http admin) requestSchema and the UPDATE_PROFILE (service) responseSchema -- i.e. these two endpoints have NEVER had schema validation applied, in production, today. Per logic-preservation discipline and explicit plan instruction (Task 7.3: 'Do NOT change business logic to fix type errors -- only add type annotations or suppressions'), fixed with casts that preserve the `undefined` resolution rather than 'correcting' the typo. Re-ran `npx tsc --noEmit` after the casts -- 0 errors. Then ran the real `npm run build` -- exit code 0. Verified dist/ output. Legacy shadowed .js files (49 under lib/, 3 at root: app.js, config.js, fruster-user-service.js) have since been DELETED (see testsNote) -- dist/ output unaffected since it's built from tsconfig's include list of .ts files, not from the deleted .js siblings.
decoratorMigrationNote: All 25 handlers converted from manual constructor DI + bus.subscribe() to @fruster/decorators (@injectable/@inject/@subscribe). tsconfig.json target changed ES2020->ES5 (with lib: [esnext, es2016]) because @fruster/decorators' injectable() wrapper does `constructor.apply(this, args)`, which throws on native ES2020+ classes -- only works on ES5-downleveled function-based classes (matches 5 sibling Fruster services). CreateUserHandler kept on manual bus.subscribe() (documented inline) because its 2 subjects use config-conditional schema getters (config.requireNames / config.withoutRequiredField) that must resolve at service-start time, not @subscribe's decoration/import time -- verified via CreateUserHandler.config.spec.js / .withoutRequiredField.config.spec.js still passing. VerifyEmailAddressHandler and ResendVerificationEmailHandler split into handle/handleHttp (shared private impl) since @subscribe keys registrations by method name and silently drops the second subject if two @subscribe calls share one method. GetMeHandler/GetProfilesByQueryHandler/UpdateProfileHandler/system/* handlers only instantiated inside their pre-existing config-conditional blocks (useMeEndpoint / profile-splitting / useDbRolesAndScopes) since @subscribe fires on instantiation. Also fixed 2 unrelated pre-existing bugs found along the way: a stray `fit()` in AddSystemRoleScopesHandler.spec.js AND a second stray `fit()` in CreateUserHandler.spec.js (both were each independently limiting the whole suite to 1 spec; the second was masked by the first until it was fixed). Completed the schemas the user originally flagged as missing: fixed REMOVE_SYSTEM_ROLE_SCOPES_REQUEST typo, fixed UPDATE_PROFILE's response schema (was reading from schemas.request instead of schemas.response), authored a new RemoveSystemRoleRequest.json (endpoint previously had no request schema at all).
runnerMigrationNote: Adopted @fruster/runner toolchain (package.json scripts: start/build/test now go through `fruster-runner`) to match fruster-push-service's modernized shape, per explicit user request with that service's package.json as reference. NOT a verbatim clone of push-service's package.json -- kept user-service's actual runtime deps (express/body-parser/cookie-parser/csprng/request for web/, @fruster/errors) and did not bump mongodb (4.17.2, driver migration is separate scope). Did bump shared tooling per explicit user choice: typescript ~5.9.3, nyc ^18, jasmine ^6.3.0, @types/node ^26, @types/jasmine ^6 added. Added @fruster/runner as a dependency (@fruster/ts-transformer comes transitively, not added directly). tsconfig.json: added `fruster.handlersPath` block, changed `include` to add `spec/**/*` (removed from exclude) since fruster-runner type-checks the whole program including specs now -- `web/` stays excluded (untouched CommonJS). Adopted mongodb-memory-server for tests per explicit user choice (in-memory Mongo instead of connecting to a real local mongod) -- new spec/support/testUtils.ts (startMongoDb/stopMongoDb/getMongoUrl, copied from push-service's pattern), spec-constants.js rewritten to spec-constants.ts with `dropDatabase: true` added (also copied from push-service) -- IMPORTANT: kept the existing positional-arg signature `testUtilsOptions(afterStart)` rather than push-service's options-object signature, since ~29 existing .spec.js files call it positionally and changing the signature would have broken all of them; this was a deliberate deviation from copying push-service verbatim. jasmine-runner.js rewritten to jasmine-runner.ts (no manual ts-node/register bridge needed -- fruster-runner registers ts-node itself). All ~29 spec files' `require('./support/spec-constants')` calls needed `.default` appended (export default interop, same rule as the rest of the migration). CRITICAL DISCOVERY: @fruster/ts-transformer (bundled in @fruster/runner) statically scans every @subscribe-decorated handler and (a) requires the `docs:` value in @subscribe(...) to be an inline object literal -- NOT a reference like `docs: docs.service.X` (throws 'Expected to find child of kind 211 in docs' -- kind 211 is ObjectLiteralExpression) -- fixed by inlining every handler's docs object (removed the `docs` import from lib/docs.ts in every handler except GetUserHandler, which still needs it for the plain-string `deprecated: docs.deprecated.GET_USER` field); (b) if a handler's parameter is typed with `FrusterRequest<T>`/response with `FrusterResponse<T>`, T MUST be a named interface/type -- an inline object type crashes schema generation (`type.getSymbol() is undefined`) since inline types have no symbol. However: if requestSchema/responseSchema is already explicitly set in @subscribe(...), the transformer skips auto-generation for that field -- but it still crashes attempting generation if FrusterRequest<InlineType> is used at all, regardless of whether requestSchema is already set (the crash happens before the skip-check). RESOLUTION: kept all 24 already-converted handlers on loose inline parameter typing (`req: { data: {...} }`, no FrusterRequest<T> wrapper) with their existing manual requestSchema/responseSchema references -- this avoids both transformer failure modes entirely since findFirstChildOfKind(param, TypeReference) never matches. One handler (system/AddSystemRoleScopesHandler.ts) had been hand-edited by the user to use `FrusterRequest<{ role: string; scopes: string[] }>` (inline type) -- reverted that one parameter back to loose inline typing (matching the other 24) since requestSchema/responseSchema were already explicit there too; documented why inline in the file. CreateUserHandler is unaffected by any of this since the transformer only visits classes with an @subscribe decorator (confirmed via fruster-transformer.js's `hasSubscribeDecorator` check) and CreateUserHandler has none. SECOND HANG MYSTERY (resolved): after fixing the transformer issues, `npm test` appeared to hang/only run 1-of-148 specs again -- spent significant effort ruling out mongodb-memory-server issues, Jasmine 5->6 version bump (bisected by pinning back to 5.4.0, ruled out), and unhandled-rejection swallowing (added process.on handlers, none fired) before finding the real cause: a SECOND pre-existing `fit()` in CreateUserHandler.spec.js (separate from the one already fixed in AddSystemRoleScopesHandler.spec.js) that had been silently masked because the other `fit()` ran first alphabetically and 'won' Jasmine's global focus lock. Verified full suite is reproducibly green across multiple clean runs after fixing it. FINAL VERIFIED STATE: `npm test` -> 148/148 SUCCESS, exit 0, nyc coverage gate passes (90%+ lines). `npm run build` -> fruster-runner ./app.ts --build succeeds, dist/ emitted. `npx fruster-runner ./app.ts` boots and connects cleanly. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING UNRELATED BUG (not fixed, out of scope, flagged only): dist/fruster-user-service.js's `require('./web/express-app')` resolves relative to dist/ at runtime, but web/ is never copied into dist/ (it's excluded from the TS build and the Dockerfile does `ADD . .` which puts web/ at the repo root, not dist/web/) -- `npm run start:dist` / the Docker image's `CMD` therefore crashes with MODULE_NOT_FOUND if expressApp.start() is ever reached. This bug pre-dates this session's changes (same broken relative path existed under the old `tsc` build too) and is unrelated to either the decorator or runner migration; flagged for a future fix, not attempted here.
testsNote:
TS-NODE BRIDGE IMPLEMENTED AND WORKING (SUPERSEDED -- see runnerMigrationNote above; this note is kept for history since it documents earlier interop fixes that are still load-bearing, e.g. the .default export rule). npm test now executes successfully end-to-end: specs compile and run against the TypeScript sources via ts-node, coverage instrumentation works, and the suite completes (no MODULE_NOT_FOUND / no compilation crash). 137/148 specs pass. `npm test` exit code is 3, caused purely by 11 failing specs (jasmine failure count) -- NOT by the nyc coverage gate, which independently passes (verified via `npx nyc report --reporter=text` showing 90.25% lines, and `npx nyc check-coverage --lines 90` exiting 0).

THE BRIDGE, STEP BY STEP (for resume-ability):
1. tsconfig.json's `exclude: [spec]` is irrelevant to spec execution -- ts-node compiles required .ts files on demand regardless of tsconfig excludes; that exclude only affects `tsc`/`npm run build`.
2. Registered ts-node at the top of spec/support/jasmine-runner.js: `require('ts-node/register/transpile-only')`, added before `const Jasmine = require('jasmine')`. transpile-only (not full type-check) was chosen deliberately so specs run even if some unrelated type issue exists deep in the reached graph -- type safety is enforced separately by `npm run build`/tsc, not by the test runner.
3. CRITICAL FINDING (empirically verified, not assumed): ts-node registration does NOT change Node's module extension resolution order. `require('../lib/constants')` with both constants.js and constants.ts present on disk resolves to constants.js regardless of ts-node being registered -- confirmed via `require.resolve()` before any fix. This is because ts-node's require hook only adds the *capability* to compile .ts, it does not reorder the .js-before-.ts precedence Node uses when both extensions exist at the same stem.
4. RESOLUTION (per explicit coordinator/user direction, received mid-task): where a .ts counterpart already exists for a module reachable from specs, the legacy .js sibling is superseded and was DELETED outright (pulled forward from the plan's Phase 9, rather than worked around via Node resolution-order tricks or a temporary .bak rename). All 52 shadowed legacy .js files were deleted: 49 under lib/**/*.js (every handler/manager/repo/model/util that has a .ts counterpart) plus 3 at root (app.js, config.js, fruster-user-service.js). Verified before deleting that every deleted stem had a corresponding .ts file already on disk (none were deleted without a .ts counterpart existing). Re-ran `npm run build` and `npm test` after deletion to confirm no regression -- results unchanged (same 137/148, same build exit 0), confirming the deletion was safe and dist/ output is unaffected (tsc builds from tsconfig's include list, not from these .js siblings).
5. Spec files had ~50 explicit-extension requires like `require('../lib/constants.js')` -- an explicit `.js` extension bypasses ts-node's extension resolution entirely (Node looks for that literal filename). Stripped the `.js` extension from all such requires across spec/*.spec.js and spec/support/*.js (mechanical, safe: verified case-by-case that no ambiguity was introduced, since post-deletion each stem has exactly one file on disk).
6. EXPORT-DEFAULT INTEROP: nearly every migrated lib/**/*.ts and root .ts file (config.ts, lib/constants.ts, lib/errors.ts, lib/deprecatedErrors.ts, lib/Publishes.ts, lib/clients/MailServiceClient.ts, lib/managers/*.ts, lib/models/*.ts, lib/repos/*.ts, lib/utils/*.ts, etc.) uses `export default X;` with no named exports. In plain CommonJS (as spec files are, and as ts-node/transpile-only compiles .ts to), `require('../lib/constants')` therefore returns `{ __esModule: true, default: {...} }`, NOT the constants object directly -- `.default` must be appended at every spec-side consumption site. This was NOT solved by choosing ts-node over dist/ (the advisor's initial framing was corrected mid-task): the .default requirement is a property of how the .ts source is written (export default), identical under ts-node and under compiled dist/ output. Fixed systematically across all spec/*.spec.js and spec/support/*.js files that require any of: lib/constants, config, lib/errors, lib/deprecatedErrors, lib/Publishes, lib/clients/MailServiceClient, lib/managers/PasswordManager, lib/managers/RoleManager, lib/models/RoleModel, lib/models/UserModel, lib/repos/RoleScopesConfigRepo, lib/repos/RoleScopesDbRepo, lib/repos/UserRepo, lib/utils/Utils -- appended `.default` at each require site (including destructured requires, e.g. `const { collections } = require('../lib/constants').default`). EXCEPTION: `fruster-user-service.ts` uses a named export `export { start, stop, createIndexes }` (confirmed via grep, no default export) -- specs requiring `../fruster-user-service` and destructuring `{ createIndexes }` need NO .default; left as-is, confirmed correct.
7. OUT-OF-PLAN-SCOPE FIX (not a new architecture fork, judged safe to fix inline): web/ was excluded from the TS migration entirely (per tsconfig.json and Phase 7's buildNote) and stays legacy CommonJS. But 4 files under web/ (web/express-app.js, web/verify-email/verify-email.index.js, web/resend-verification-email/resend-verification-email.index.js, web/set-password/set-password.index.js) still required the OLD unscoped packages `fruster-log` / `fruster-bus`, which are no longer installed (removed org-wide by this migration). This broke both `npm start` (production) and spec execution (fruster-user-service.ts requires ./web/express-app at module load time), independent of the ts-node-vs-dist test-execution decision -- i.e. this was an objectively incomplete migration, not a scope question with multiple defensible answers. Fixed all 4: `fruster-log` -> `@fruster/log` (no .default needed -- confirmed @fruster/log is plain `module.exports = ...`), `fruster-bus` -> `@fruster/bus` with `.default` appended (confirmed @fruster/bus's main export is `exports.default = ...`). Also fixed those same 3 web/*.index.js files' `require('../../lib/constants')` and `require('../../config')` (and one destructured `{ passwordValidationRegex }` from config) to append `.default`, same interop rule as spec files.
8. Verified DB isolation is NOT a regression from this work: spec/support/spec-constants.js's testUtilsOptions never set `dropDatabase: true` in @fruster/test-utils' startBeforeEach options, even before this migration (confirmed via `git show HEAD:spec/support/spec-constants.js` -- identical, pre-existing). @fruster/test-utils' startBeforeEach only calls connection.db.dropDatabase() when options.dropDatabase is truthy (confirmed by reading node_modules/@fruster/test-utils/dist/index.js source). This is pre-existing suite behavior, not something the ts-node bridge broke.

REMAINING 11 FAILING SPECS (out of 148; same 11 reproduce consistently across 3 full-suite runs, including runs preceded by a manual `db.dropDatabase()` on fruster-user-service-test): AddSystemRoleScopesHandler (2 specs, SYSTEM_ROLE_ALREADY_EXISTS 'padmin'), CreateUserHandler 'should validate indexed duplicates email' (E11000 dup key firstName_1), GetSystemRolesHandler 'should be possible to get all roles with config format' (SYSTEM_ROLE_ALREADY_EXISTS), GetUsersByAggregateHandler (2 specs, E11000 dup key email_1), GetUsersByQueryHandler 'expanded profile w/ old user data' (count assertions off: expected 5 got 7/3), RemoveSystemRoleHandler + RemoveSystemRoleScopesHandler (SYSTEM_ROLE_ALREADY_EXISTS), RoleManager 'should save roles from config to database if database is empty' (TypeError reading '0' -- roles['super-admin'] is undefined), UpdateUserHandler 'resend verification mail ... emailVerificationTemplateByRole' (Email is not unique). Fingerprint strongly suggests ONE root cause across most of them: no per-test DB reset (dropDatabase never configured, see point 8), so tests that assume a clean/empty DB or unique fixture names (e.g. role name 'padmin') collide with state left by earlier specs in the SAME suite run (spec/support/jasmine.json's spec_files glob always loads and runs the full suite -- the jasmine-runner.js CLI arg for a single spec file does NOT actually isolate execution to that file, confirmed empirically). This is test-isolation / fixture-design territory (Phase 6 / test-fixer scope per the workflow's Test Fixing phase), not a migration-bridging gap -- the bridge itself (module resolution, compilation, coverage) is fully proven working by the 137 passing specs across every handler/manager/repo category. Recommend Phase 6 test-fixer investigate: (a) whether adding `dropDatabase: true` to spec-constants.js's testUtilsOptions is safe/intended (would fix the SYSTEM_ROLE_ALREADY_EXISTS and E11000 cluster), and (b) the RoleManager and GetUsersByQueryHandler count-mismatch failures individually, as they may be genuine assertion/fixture bugs rather than pollution.
